strings.name: Tadao Ando
strings.summary: Ando entered architecture through travel, observation and self-education. Exposed concrete, geometric walls and light organize spaces that are inward-looking yet open to nature. Row House in Sumiyoshi and Church of the Light reorder everyday experience; Naoshima’s museums connect art, terrain and movement. He also transformed a historic Paris building. The 1995 Pritzker laureate continues exploring freedom within constraints and the public significance of cultural spaces.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 2026-11-13. Selected milestones span 1941–2026; this is not a complete catalogue or live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Built global influence through architecture using exposed concrete, light and space, while contributing to cultural facilities and urban-environment projects.

strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Self-taught in architecture through travel, reading and direct observation
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Light organizes space
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Church of the Light uses a simple concrete volume and cruciform opening to place changing natural light at the center of architectural experience.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Art, terrain and movement
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Chichu and Naoshima’s new museum connect the display of art with terrain, daylight and routes of movement.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Reflects on a practice of building with light
strings.timeline.event-01.text: In a Whitewall interview from his Osaka studio, he discussed geometry, materials and human experience, including the new Naoshima museum.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Naoshima New Museum of Art opens
strings.timeline.event-02.text: His tenth structure for Benesse Art Site Naoshima uses layered spaces and daylight to display contemporary art from Japan and Asia.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Bourse de Commerce transformation opens
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Working with French restoration and architectural teams, a concrete cylinder was inserted into the historic building to create dialogue with contemporary art.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Chichu Art Museum opens on Naoshima
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Mostly embedded in the landscape, the museum uses daylight and specific spaces for works by Monet, James Turrell and others.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Receives the Pritzker Architecture Prize
strings.timeline.event-05.text: The award recognized rich experiences created through restrained geometry, materials and light, alongside his independently developed practice.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Church of the Light is completed
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Concrete walls and a cruciform opening form a place of worship in Ibaraki, Osaka, intensifying awareness of body and setting through daylight.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Row House in Sumiyoshi wins an architecture award
strings.timeline.event-07.text: The compact house’s open courtyard divides domestic spaces, bringing rain, light and movement into urban living; it received Japan’s architecture institute award.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Establishes his Osaka practice
strings.timeline.event-08.text: After travel and self-education, his independent office began with houses, developing an exploration of concrete, geometry and nature.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Born in Osaka
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Born in Osaka and raised by his grandmother, he encountered local craftsmanship, briefly boxed and later taught himself architecture.
